name: Asteroid Main Belt
story: A ring of rocky leftovers between Mars and Jupiter — 2.2 to 3.2 AU. Hundreds of thousands of bodies catalogued; total estimated mass less than 4% of the Moon. Not the densely-packed asteroid field of science fiction: typical spacing between objects is about 1 million kilometres. The belt never accreted into a planet because Jupiter's gravity kept stirring the orbits, preventing collisions from sticking. Three Kirkwood gaps mark resonances with Jupiter where asteroids get cleared out.
comparison: If you stood on Ceres (the largest body) you'd struggle to see another asteroid without a telescope. The belt's total mass is roughly the mass of Pluto.
